componentPlan.focusQuote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Models the convention process in taught order from convening through revising to signing.

componentPlan.focusQuote: Among the chief points at issue were how much power to allow the central government
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks recall of central facts about purpose, quorum needs, and debated issues.

overview.headline: How delegates drafted the United States Constitution in 1787

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the document signed in 1787 established the government of the United States.
keyPoints.quote: signed on September 17, 1787, established the government of the United States.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the convention convened in Philadelphia in 1787 to revise earlier governing articles.
keyPoints.quote: convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787

keyPoints.point: Students learn that members adjourned daily until a quorum of seven states was obtained.
keyPoints.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that debate led delegates to draft an entirely new frame of government instead of amending.
keyPoints.quote: it became clear by mid-June that, rather than amend the existing Articles, the Convention would draft an entirely new frame of government.

keyTerms.gloss: Meeting of delegates that drafted a new frame of government in secret sessions
keyTerms.quote: Drafted in secret by delegates to the Constitutional Convention during the summer of 1787

keyTerms.gloss: Earlier system that delegates met to revise before drafting a new plan
keyTerms.quote: to revise the Articles of Confederation.

keyTerms.gloss: Minimum attendance of seven states needed to conduct business
keyTerms.quote: until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25.

keyTerms.gloss: National authority whose power was debated by Convention delegates
keyTerms.quote: how much power to allow the central government

analysis.pageCoverage: Explains why the Federal Convention met in Philadelphia and how delegates moved from revising the Articles to drafting and signing a new Constitution.
analysis.subject: civics
